_comment: Tier-2 for dune::linear_elasticity#3, #4 and #6 — mu and lam are dune.ufl.Constants, so the swap and the plane-stress substitution are VALUE changes that cost no rebuild and only two modules are compiled (the sym(grad(u)) form and the bare-grad(u) one). Wall time 5 s warm, 310 s cold (2026-08-06, dune-fem 2.12.0.2). Uniaxial pull on a 32x32 dimRange=2 Q1 grid, E=210e9, nu=0.3, t=1e6: u_x(1) = 4.340198e-06 and min(u_y) = -1.859393e-06, i.e. the lateral contraction is NEGATIVE under tension, which is the sign detector #3 asks for. Judged against the plane-STRESS value t/E = 4.761905e-06 the ratio is 0.9114 against 1-nu^2 = 0.9100 — the run looks ~9% too SOFT, confirming the direction the catalog corrected; substituting lam_ps = 2*mu*lam/(lam+2*mu) brings the ratio to 1.0016. Swapping mu and lam still converged and still printed a plausible 3.306729e-06. For #4: a rigid-body rotation interpolated into the space gives inner(sym(grad(u)),sym(grad(u))) integrated = 2.31e-36, i.e. zero, while inner(grad(u),grad(u)) gives 2.000000e-06 — bare grad(u) invents strain in a pure rotation — and the wrong FORM still assembles and solves. GRID NOTE: the 0.9114 ratio is discretisation-sensitive; at 8x8 it reads 0.9330 and the assertion band of 0.02 fails. Grid resolution is not part of the generated code, so refining to 32x32 is free.
